correctness.rationale: A quotient weak core must be T0 by reduction to the Kolmogorov quotient and beat-free since a beat-point retraction is a proper quotient homotopy equivalence. Any two non-homeomorphic reachable cores from a source of at most six points both have at most five points: a same-size quotient is a homeomorphism and an irreducible source cannot have another core. Independently, a beat-free poset on at most five points has no three-element chain: a middle point would need at least two upper and two lower covers, exhausting the other points, and then each lower cover has that middle point as its sole upper cover. Each nonsingleton height-two component has minimum degree two, so on at most five points the only such graphs are K2,2 and K2,3, with the allowable level orientations; an extra isolated point can accompany K2,2. Their weak types leave only P2,3 and P3,2 as the distinct pair, both genuinely quotient-minimal since no <=4-point model has connected rank-two first homology, even after Kolmogorov reduction. A source of at most five points cannot quotient onto both. Independently rebuilt the final topology on all pair identifications of all 4824 naturally labelled six-point orders by intersecting the saturated open downsets, not by replaying the supplied preorder closure. The 33 double-target orders are connected and height two, with 22,10,1 occurrences of one isomorphism class each at seven, eight, nine edges, respectively. Only seven edges give graph rank two. The sole pair onto P2,3 is {1,2}, and onto P3,2 is {4,5}, in the frozen labelling. In the first map the given source spanning tree maps onto the target tree and the two non-tree edges correspond bijectively. Hence the map on fundamental groups is an isomorphism, not just on Betti ranks; the dual symmetry gives the second map. McCord naturality transfers the graph weak equivalences to the quotient maps.
residual_risks: Kernel uniqueness counts partitions, not distinct maps to a labelled target. The classification applies only through six source points and only to minimal weak-equivalence quotients.

value.rationale: Nonuniqueness of the natural irreducible weak-quotient construction motivates the size cutoff. The independent classification shows that two different quotient cores at the first possible size force one specific common source and one partition per core, answering rigidity questions left by the existence example. This distinguishes the phenomenon from simply counting low-order finite models of a wedge.
residual_risks: No classification is inferred for bigger sources or for notions of weak core not defined by final-topology quotients.
